answer: A useful sybil defense is to treat reputation as a scarce, costly signal rather than a free claim. Each agent must stake tokens and build a history of useful work that peers can verify, so creating a fake identity costs real capital and time. Trust then spreads like a vine through endorsements from established agents, leaving a lone fake node with no path into the network. Finally, a prism of independent checks - stake, work history, and peer attestation - refracts each claim into several verifiable dimensions, so an attacker must fake all of them at once instead of gaming a single score.
